title: Technician – 6557 Posts
qualification: For Technician Grade-I Signal, candidates need a Bachelor of Science in Physics/Electronics/Computer Science/Information Technology/Instrumentation, a three-year diploma in Engineering, or a Degree in Engineering in these streams. For most Technician Grade-III posts, candidates need Matriculation /SSLC plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT or Matriculation/SSLC plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in the relevant trade (such as Fitter, Welder, Electrician, Machinist, Carpenter, or Blacksmith, depending on the post applied for).
salary: Candidates curious about RRB Technician in-hand salary should note that pay depends on the post and pay level assigned. Technician Grade-I Signal carries a higher starting pay than Technician Grade-III posts, as shown below. || Selected candidates will undergo training wherever prescribed, during which only a stipend is paid rather than full pay.
age_limit: Candidates from reserved categories get standard relaxation in the upper age limit: 5 years for SC/ST , 3 years for OBC-NCL , and additional relaxation for PwBD candidates (10 years for UR/EWS, 13 years for OBC-NCL, 15 years for SC/ST). Ex-servicemen get age relaxation equal to their length of service plus 3 years (UR/EWS), 6 years (OBC-NCL), or 8 years (SC/ST) after deducting service length from their actual age.
application_fee: The application fee for RRB Technician CEN 02/2026 differs by candidate category and is partially refundable for those who appear in the CBT. General category candidates pay more than reserved categories, with both fee structures eligible for partial refund upon attending the exam. || Fee payment is accepted only through online mode - internet banking, debit/credit cards, or UPI. Applications submitted without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected, so candidates must pay the fee before 31 July 2026.
selection_process: Candidates often ask how RRB selects Technicians, and the answer is a three-stage process based purely on merit. The recruitment involves a Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification (DV), and a Medical Examination, with shortlisting at each stage determined by performance in the previous one. || Computer Based Test (CBT):A single CBT of 90 minutes with 100 questions and negative marking of 1/3rd mark per wrong answer. Minimum qualifying marks are 40% (UR/EWS), 30% (OBC-NCL/SC), and 25% (ST). || Document Verification (DV):Candidates are shortlisted at a 1:1 ratio against vacancies based on CBT merit, RRB-wise. Original documents must be produced; no extra time is given for missing certificates. || Medical Examination (ME):Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities as per the medical standard (A3, B1, B2, or C1) prescribed for the specific post. || Based on typical RRB recruitment cycles, CBT is expected a few months after the application closes, followed by DV and medical examination in subsequent phases - though exact dates will be announced on official RRB websites.

age_limit: The minimum and maximum age, as on the closing date of online application (3 August 2026), must be 18 years and 28 years respectively. The cut-off date for determining age, qualifications, and claims of SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/EWS/PwBD status or any other benefit (fee exemption, reservation, age relaxation, etc.), where not specified otherwise, is the last date for submission of online application, i.e., 3 August 2026. || Additional permissible relaxation in upper age limit for Group ‘C’ posts: || Key conditions on age relaxation: || No age relaxation is allowed to SC/ST/OBC candidates applying against unreserved posts. || SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates must upload a copy of the certificate in the prescribed format, duly signed by the competent authority. OBC candidates must produce the Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) certificate valid for appointment to posts under the Central Government, and must ensure they do not fall in the creamy layer as on 3 August 2026. || Age relaxation for Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) is given only to candidates with 40% or more disability holding a valid certificate. As per Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment O.M. No. 18-25/2024-Policy dated 17 December 2025, disability conditions falling under "likely to improve" (temporary disability category) are not eligible for reservation, while conditions that are "progressive, non-progressive, or not likely to improve" are eligible. Candidates with a temporary disability certificate bearing conditions other than "likely to improve" must get themselves re-assessed under the RPwD Amendment Rules 2024. || Candidates claiming age relaxation as a widow, divorced woman, or woman judicially separated from her husband must produce specific documentary evidence (death certificate with affidavit of non-remarriage for widows; certified copy of the court judgment/decree along with an affidavit of non-remarriage for divorced/judicially separated women) issued by the competent authority.
application_fee: A non-refundable fee of Rs 500 is mandatory for applicants other than Ex-Servicemen, SC, ST, Women, and PwBD candidates, who are exempted from the fee. || The fee must be deposited online throughState Bank Collect (SBI Collect)only; fees paid through any other mode will not be accepted, and the application will be treated as without fee and rejected. || The transaction number/receipt number generated after successful payment must be mentioned at the appropriate place in the online application before submission. || Candidates must download the e-receipt from SBI Collect and upload it in the online application, and are advised to preserve it for future reference. || A candidate can apply for multiple post codes subject to fulfilling eligibility criteria for each; primary/registration details need to be submitted only once, but the application form (except registration details) must be filled and the fee paid separately for each post code. || Fee once paid will not be refunded on any count, and the application once finally submitted cannot be withdrawn or modified.
selection_process: Selection is a three-stage process: screening of applications, a qualifying Trade Test, and a Competitive Written Examination. This section explains the marking scheme and qualifying criteria for the written stage. || Online applications received within the stipulated last date are screened by a duly constituted Screening Committee, which shortlists candidates for a Trade Test in the relevant trade. The Trade Test isqualifying in nature; its syllabus will be notified separately on the official website. || Candidates who qualify in the Trade Test are called for the Competitive Written Examination.
